Annotation Interface GlobalTable

@Documented @Retention(RUNTIME) @Target(TYPE) public @interface GlobalTable
Declares that the annotated entity's table should have the CockroachDB GLOBAL locality — optimized for low-latency reads from every region, at the cost of slower writes. Reference/lookup tables (currencies, feature flags, product catalogs) are the usual candidates.

This annotation is declared intent only: it does not change the schema. Your migrations still own ALTER TABLE ... SET LOCALITY GLOBAL. Pair it with Crdb.verifyLocality(DataSource, Class...) to check, at an explicit point you choose, that the live table actually matches the annotation (and to get the exact fix-up SQL when it does not).

An entity must not carry both @GlobalTable and RegionalByRow; that is a contradiction the check always reports.

Table-name resolution. Because this is a low-level JDBC library with no ORM metamodel, the table name defaults to the entity's simple class name, folded to lower case the way CockroachDB folds an unquoted identifier (so Currency resolves to currency). There is no camelCase-to-snake_case conversion: if your table is feature_flags but your class is FeatureFlag, set table() explicitly. The value may be schema-qualified ("app.currencies") and may use double-quotes for names that need them ("\"Currency\"").
